Richard Ferri emphasizes that rather than relying on active investment strategies—such as market timing and stock picking, which are complex and often yield disappointing returns—a better approach is to use passive investment vehicles like index funds and ETFs. These allow investors to participate in the market at relatively low costs. More importantly, in addition to choosing low-cost, index-based investment products, investors should maintain a fixed (passive strategy) asset allocation and rebalance periodically when appropriate. This approach helps to maximize wealth returns with the lowest cost and minimal risk
